Your LinkedIn content is the ad and your profile is the landing page. A member of our community fixed the keywords in his headline and his next post did 8,000 views, up from a 1,000 view ceiling he kept hitting. A consultant with 20,000 followers rewrote his headline and about section, changed nothing about his posts, and saw reach up 226%, engagement up 327%, and a lead the same day. Before a human ever does the 10 second gut check on your page, LinkedIn’s algorithm has already read five profile fields to decide who sees your post at all. We set four of those once, when we opened the account, and never touched them again.

This video covers every section of a LinkedIn profile in the order a buyer’s eyes move: photo, banner, headline, about, featured, custom button, services, and work history. It walks through the five fields LinkedIn’s engineering team confirmed the algorithm reads (name, headline, company, industry, title), the what-who-proof headline formula with examples across SaaS, consulting, and technical niches, the search bar that brought Distinctiva a $20,000 a month client, the testimonial move inside the services section, the link trick inside your experience entries, and profiles from Anthony Pierri, Lara Acosta, and Jake Ward that each handle the formula differently.

WHAT YOU’LL LEARN:
 The five profile fields LinkedIn reads before it shows your post to anyone
 Why your industry dropdown can send the algorithm a mixed signal
 The what-who-proof formula for a headline that works for machines and humans
 The four character word that gets you shortlisted for speaking slots
 Four elements of a banner and the corner nothing important can sit in
 A 10 line about section structure with five jobs
 Why a pinned viral post is the wrong thing in your featured section
 Two exit doors on your profile almost nobody opens

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 LinkedIn’s algorithm reads five fields on every post: name, headline, company, industry, and title
 Your headline follows you into every post and every comment, so it is the highest value text on your profile
 A headline needs what you help someone do, who you help, and one proof point
 Your profile has four jobs: one talks to the machine, three talk to a human in a fixed order of clarity, trust, then a step into your world
 The featured section exists to move someone off LinkedIn and onto a list, a booking page, or a lead magnet you own
 The services section is searchable, and testimonials inside it put other people’s words on your page instead of yours
 Headline first, then industry and title, then featured and custom button: the fix takes 20 minutes
